$doc: Vyomi capability registry — Azure Function Apps (Microsoft.Web/sites, kind=functionapp). One entry per console feature/section; level per substrate (nano = shared core, also dev_server/unified ingress; offline = appliance). Proven by tests/conformance/test_capabilities.py.

azure.functionapp.function.invoke.title: Function Test/Run (real sandboxed execution)
limitations: Only the Python programming model (a `main(req)` entry point) runs.
The sandbox is restricted (no filesystem, network or process access, a curated stdlib subset) — the same technique as the Lambda console's Invoke.

azure.functionapp.appsettings.title: App settings and connection strings (Environment variables)

azure.functionapp.keys.title: App keys (host keys, system keys, function keys)

azure.functionapp.scale.title: Scale and concurrency (Flex Consumption)
limitations: A configured capacity of exactly zero (maximumInstanceCount x perInstanceConcurrency) is ENFORCED: every invoke is rejected (429 FunctionsTooBusy), the same way a real scaled-to-zero Flex Consumption app never has an instance available to run on.

Instance memory and any positive maximum instance count / per-instance concurrency are stored on the site and returned from the API exactly as configured, but never enforced against concurrent callers — Vyomi runs every invoke synchronously (nothing to run concurrently), so no invoke is ever rejected for exceeding a nonzero capacity.

azure.functionapp.locks.title: Resource locks
limitations: Lock create/list/delete are real Microsoft.Authorization/locks over ARM; this blade manages the locks scoped to this function app only (no scope switch). A lock on the app, or on its resource group or subscription, really blocks writes/deletes with 409 ScopeLocked (a CanNotDelete lock blocks deletes only).

azure.functionapp.publishprofile.title: Download / reset publish profile
limitations: The profile is a simulator-generated credential; it does not grant real deployment access and Vyomi has no Web Deploy / Kudu endpoint behind it.

azure.functionapp.rbac.title: Access control (IAM) — role assignments and role definitions
limitations: Role assignments and role definitions are the generic subscription-scoped Microsoft.Authorization store (shared with every other Azure resource), not filtered to assignments scoped exactly to this function app.
Deny assignments and classic administrators are always empty (Vyomi models neither).

azure.functionapp.activitylog.title: Activity log
limitations: Only console/SDK-triggered mutations made since the simulation booted are recorded (no historical backfill); severity/category filtering and the 7/30/90-day timespan picker are not modelled, and `caller` is a fixed placeholder identity rather than the real signed-in principal.

azure.functionapp.defender.title: Microsoft Defender for Cloud (this function app's recommendations)
limitations: Shows the live Defender for Cloud recommendations for this resource from Vyomi's rule engine (see azure.defender.recommendations); Azure's full built-in recommendation catalogue is not reproduced.

azure.functionapp.identity.title: Identity (system-assigned managed identity)
limitations: User assigned identities are real: the identity block can reference Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/userAssignedIdentities resources, an unknown reference is rejected with 400 ResourceNotFound and the attached identity's principalId/clientId are resolved from that resource.

azure.functionapp.customdomains.title: Custom domains (hostNameBindings)
limitations: Adding a domain never verifies real DNS ownership (no TXT/CNAME lookup) — any hostname is accepted.
An SNI/IP SSL binding mints a deterministic, simulator-only certificate thumbprint (see Certificates); no real certificate is issued.

azure.functionapp.certificates.title: Certificates
limitations: Vyomi has no Microsoft.Web/certificates resource or real PKI — a certificate only exists for a custom domain that has an SNI/IP SSL binding, and its thumbprint is a deterministic simulator value, not a real issued certificate.

azure.functionapp.cors.title: CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing)
limitations: Only the Origin header is checked against the allowed-origins list; Vyomi does not simulate a real browser preflight (OPTIONS) round-trip or emit Access-Control-* response headers.

azure.functionapp.networking.title: Networking (public network access, VNet integration)
limitations: Disabling public network access IS enforced: every invoke is rejected (403) exactly as a real app with no private endpoint would reject public callers.
VNet integration and private endpoints are stored and returned from the API exactly as configured, but never enforced — Vyomi has no virtual network data plane to route traffic through.

azure.functionapp.authentication.title: Authentication (Easy Auth)
limitations: authsettingsV2 round-trips with real validation (Entra registration clientId/issuer, allowed audiences, excluded paths, secret setting must exist) and the function front door enforces unauthenticatedClientAction (302 to the Entra authorize URL, 401, 403, AllowAnonymous). A credential is the simulator bearer token or a JWT whose claims (exp, aud, tenant) validate; the JWT signature is not verified (Vyomi's Entra issues opaque tokens) and there is no interactive browser sign-in or Google/Facebook/Apple providers.

azure.functionapp.diagnosticsettings.title: Diagnostic settings
limitations: Vyomi stores and returns the destination/category configuration exactly as configured (a real ARM extension resource), but never actually delivers logs or metrics to the configured Log Analytics workspace / storage account / Event Hub — there is no telemetry pipeline behind it.

azure.functionapp.telemetry.title: Metrics, Logs, Log stream, Events (preview)
limitations: Every row is a REAL recorded invocation (timestamp, function, HTTP status, measured duration) appended by the sandboxed invoke path — never synthetic/random data.
Log stream and Events (preview) poll this same recorded list on a refresh, rather than a live push/websocket stream or a real Event Grid system topic.
No historical backfill: only invocations made since the simulation booted are recorded, capped at the most recent 200.

azure.functionapp.alerts.title: Alerts (metric alert rules)
limitations: Alert rules are the generic Microsoft.Insights/metricAlerts store (core/azure_monitor_core.py), scoped to this app via `properties.scopes`.

Vyomi stores rules but does not run a continuous metric-evaluation loop; the panel computes a current value on demand from the real recorded invocation log and compares it to the rule's threshold, rather than firing/resolving in real time.

azure.functionapp.healthcheck.title: Health check
limitations: "Run health check now" resolves the configured path to a function by name and runs it through the real invoke sandbox; it does not continuously probe the app or load-balance across instances the way real Azure's health check does.

azure.functionapp.advisor.title: Advisor recommendations
limitations: A small, fixed rule set evaluated live against this app's real configuration and real recent invocation outcomes — not Azure Advisor's full recommendation catalogue.

azure.functionapp.diagnosedetectors.title: Diagnose and solve problems
limitations: A small, fixed set of real health detectors (app state, recent failure rate, scale capacity, public network access) — not Azure's full detector catalogue or its guided troubleshooters.

azure.functionapp.resourcehealth.title: Resource health
limitations: Availability is derived from the app's real `state` and lock status, not a historical uptime feed or platform-level health events.

azure.functionapp.resourcevisualizer.title: Resource visualizer
limitations: Shows this app's real linked resource references (App Service plan, the storage account named in AzureWebJobsStorage, the Application Insights key) as a list, not an interactive dependency diagram.

azure.functionapp.appfiles.title: App files
limitations: Read-only: shows the app's real stored function code and bindings (and a host.json synthesised from real runtime/scale settings) — there is no writable Kudu VFS or deployment zip behind it.

azure.functionapp.applicationinsights.title: Application Insights
limitations: A real Microsoft.Insights/components resource linked through the app's connection string; requests / failures / dependencies / events / traces are read from the OTLP-ingested trace + log store (and requests Vyomi measured for the app). No Kusto query engine, Live Metrics stream or Application Map.

azure.functionapp.deploymentcenter.title: Deployment Center
limitations: Real ARM control plane plus real deployments through the shared CI seam (core/ci_core.py): sourcecontrols/web (repo URL, branch, manual/continuous integration, GitHub Actions with a generated workflow YAML; scmType maintained), deployments + log, publishing credentials and basic-auth policies. Local Git (scmType LocalGit): a push (POST .../localgit, a Vyomi extension of the Kudu git receiver; with the Gitea git host (offline, VYOMI_CI_GITEA=1) a real git clone URL and real `git push`) commits to the app's repo, builds, and records a Success/Failed deployment with the build log. GitHub source: the branch tarball is fetched (public, or private with the user's own personal access token entered in the Deployment Center; stored server-side, never shown) and built on the offline appliance; on Nano there is no outbound HTTP so a GitHub sync is a Failed deployment saying so (Local Git works on Nano). Azure Repos / Bitbucket / generic git cannot be fetched (no HTTP git client) and are recorded Failed with that reason. The build produces a content-addressed package artifact (Dockerfile validated; container image builds use BuildKit on the offline appliance only); the App Service runtime does not hot-swap to the deployed package, the GitHub Actions workflow is generated and, when a personal access token is supplied (properties.vyomiAccessToken; offline appliance only - Nano cannot reach GitHub), committed to the connected repository through the GitHub Contents API (without a token it is generated but not committed; the pipeline itself runs on GitHub), and OAuth account authorization is not performed (PAT only).

azure.functionapp.extensions.title: Extensions (site extensions)
limitations: Site extensions install from the same bundled gallery as App Service (Windows function apps only; Linux returns 400 as in Azure): install/uninstall records state and a marker file, and the extension's own code is never downloaded or run.

azure.functionapp.apimanagement.title: API Management integration
limitations: Linking an API Management instance (siteConfig.apiManagementConfig.id = the service or .../apis/{api}) IMPORTS the Function App's API into that gateway: an API with one GET and one POST operation per function whose backend is the app (resolved in-process), kept in step when functions are added or removed; unlinking removes it. Requests through the gateway (subscription key, policies, rate limits) are really forwarded to the function and its output returned. Web Apps import a wildcard API. OpenAPI/Swagger definition import is not performed.

azure.functionapp.kudu.title: Advanced Tools (Kudu): environment, settings, deployments, tool links
limitations: Served as an ARM extension under sites/{site}/kudu/api, not as a separate https://{site}.scm.azurewebsites.net host, so the real Kudu dashboard UI and its Git/zip-deploy endpoints are not served there.
Settings (SCM_*) are stored and read back; they do not change Kudu behaviour.

azure.functionapp.console.title: Console (Kudu command console over the function app's files and app settings)
limitations: No operating-system process sits behind the simulated function app, so programs cannot be executed; the interpreter covers file, environment and process-listing commands only (pwd cd ls cat echo head tail wc grep mkdir touch rm cp mv env ps tree find, pipes, > and >>). Writes are real edits to the app's file store; the sandboxed function code is not hot-reloaded.

azure.functionapp.appeditor.title: App Service Editor (edit the function app's files)
limitations: Edits the app's virtual file system (function sources, host.json, logs); edits persist but the sandboxed runtime does not hot-swap to them. No debugging or Git integration.

azure.functionapp.processes.title: Process explorer (processes of the function host)
limitations: The process table is MODELLED from the app's real state (host worker per instance, the Kudu process); CPU time is the sum of measured invocation durations. It is not an OS process table: no kill/dump/profile actions.

azure.functionapp.logstream.title: Log stream (live tail of the function app's logs)
limitations: Tails real recorded lines (function invocations, deployments, lifecycle and console actions) by polling every 2 seconds; there is no always-on stdout because the app runs no persistent process.

azure.functionapp.serviceconnector.title: Service Connector
limitations: Creating a connection validates the target in this subscription and writes the real connection app settings (endpoint, plus a generated secret for secret auth); no network path, firewall rule or role assignment is created for the target.

azure.functionapp.tasks.title: Tasks (Automation)
limitations: Tasks are real Logic App workflows (Recurrence trigger plus Http-to-ARM actions, core/azure_tasks_core.py): scheduled runs call the simulator's own ARM and keep results in the run output; only Recurrence triggers and Http/Compose actions run, there is no e-mail or Teams connector, and Nano only fires schedules while the tab is open.

azure.functionapp.bindingseditor.title: Function Integration (bindings editor)
limitations: Bindings are stored as the function's function.json and returned by the API; the HTTP trigger and the Cosmos DB change-feed trigger (cosmosDBTrigger, run inline on each write) are executed; queue/blob/timer/service bus triggers never fire and output bindings write nothing.

azure.functionapp.invocations.title: Invocations (per-function invocation history)
limitations: Lists the real invoke attempts Vyomi ran for this function (status, measured duration, error); the history is capped at the last 200 invocations per app and there is no Application Insights trace or per-invocation log lines.
